title: Hirayasumi TV Anime to Stream on Netflix
content:
Viz Media announced on Monday that the television anime of Keigo Shinzō 's Hirayasumi manga (a co-production with Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions Co., Ltd and Production +h. ) will stream internationally on Netflix in January. The anime's staff also announced on Monday that Gen Hoshino is performing the anime's opening theme song.

Viz Media describes the human drama story:

With a carefree outlook on life, Hiroto knows better than anyone that slowing down is sometimes the best way to move forward. At 29 years old, carefree Hiroto Ikuta doesn't have a girlfriend, a full-time job, or a plan for the future—and he couldn't be happier. Hiroto's breezy attitude isn't easy for everyone to understand, though. In a world filled with anxiety, confusion, and grief, Hiroto and the people who surround him are all just doing their best to figure out this thing called life. After developing an unlikely friendship with the grouchy old woman who lives in his neighborhood, Hiroto suddenly finds himself inheriting not just her house but some rather difficult emotions as well. His 18-year-old cousin, Natsumi, moves in with him, but as a struggling art student, she has her own troubles to deal with and may just put Hiroto's easygoing lifestyle to the test.

The anime stars:

• Yūma Uchida as Hiroto Ikuta

• Mayu Takahashi as Natsumi Kobayashi

• Rikako Aikawa as Hanae Wada

• Daisuke Namikawa as Hideki Noguchi

• Yōko Hikasa as Yomogi Tachibana

• Yume Miyamoto as Akari Yokoyama

• Yūichirō Umehara as Ryō Ishikawa

• Japanese television announcer Yūko Naitō as Narrator

Kei Suezawa ( Fate/Grand Order The Movie Divine Realm of the Round Table: Camelot - Wandering: Agateram, FLCL Progressive ) is directing the anime at Production +h. Naoyuki Asano (2022 Urusei Yatsura , Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! , Mr. Osomatsu ) is designing the characters. Mika Nishimura ( Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction , Typhoon Noruda ) is the art director. Kaori Sawada ( What Did You Eat Yesterday? , When Spring Comes ) is composing the music. TOMOO will perform the anime's ending theme song "Fūmizekka" (Delicious Flavor).

The anime will premiere in January 2027 in Japan on the NHK General channel.

Viz Media and Japan Society hosted the world premiere screening of the first episode at Japan Society's location in New York City on October 7.

Shinzō launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Weekly Big Comic Spirits magazine in April 2021. Shogakukan published the manga's 10th compiled book volume on April 30, and the series has over 1.1 million copies in circulation worldwide. The manga will end on November 16. Viz Media is releasing the manga in English.

The manga also inspired a live-action series , which premiered on NHK in November 2025.
author: ANN

title: Live-Action Golden Kamuy: Karafuto Pursuit Arc Series Unveils More Cast
content:
The official website for Golden Kamuy : Karafuto Tsuiseki-hen (Gol den Kamuy: Karafuto Pursuit Arc), the new live-action series based on Satoru Noda 's Golden Kamuy manga, unveiled two more cast members as well as a new key visual for the series on Monday.

The newly announced cast members are:

Ayana Shiramoto as Sofia Golden Hand

Hiroto Ōshita as Kirawus

Kenji Katagiri is returning to direct the new series alongside new director Masaaki Yoshimura . Tetsuo Kamata (live-action BLUE LOCK film) is the new scriptwriter. Yutaka Yamada and Yoshiaki Dewa are returning to compose the music. Hiroshi Nakagawa and Debo Akibe are again serving as the Ainu language and cultural advisers. CREDEUS is again producing the series.

The live-action series will debut streaming on WOWOW on January 24.

The first live-action Golden Kamuy film opened in Japan in January 2024 and topped the Japanese box office in its first weekend. The film sold 356,000 tickets for 533,848,690 yen (about US$3.44 million in current conversion) in its first three days. Netflix began streaming the first film in May 2024.

Shigeaki Kubo directed the first film at production company CREDEUS . Tsutomu Kuroiwa wrote the script. Yutaka Yamada composed the music. Hiroshi Nakagawa and Debo Akibe were credited as Ainu culture advisers.

Kenji Katagiri , Ken Ochiai , and Yōsuke Satō joined the film's director Kubo on directing the follow-up Golden Kamuy -The Hunt of Prisoners in Hokkaido- live-action series . Similarly, Yoshiaki Dewa joined the film's composer Yamada for the series. Japanese rock group ACIDMAN performed the theme song "Kagayakerumono" (Those Who Shine). The live-action series debuted in October 2024, and Netflix added the series in February 2025.

Kento Yamazaki reprises his role as Saichi Sugimoto and Anna Yamada as Asirpa. Yū Inaba , Sōkō Wada , and Tetta Sugimoto joined the film's cast as Tokishige Usami, Toshiyuki Kadokura, and Anji Toni, respectively.

Kenji Katagiri directed the film at CREDEUS based on a script by returning writer Tsutomu Kuroiwa . Yutaka Yamada was also back to compose the music, and Hiroshi Nakagawa and Debo Akibe served as Ainu culture and language supervisors.

Rock band 10-FEET performed the theme song "Kowarete Kieru made" (Until It Breaks and Disappears).

Noda launched the manga in Shueisha 's Young Jump magazine in 2014, and ended it in April 2022. The manga has inspired four anime seasons. The show's final arc premiered on January 5, and will continue this winter with the climactic "Runaway Train" arc.

title: Fool Night Manga Crosses 1 Million Copies Worldwide
content:
Viz Media licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

Kamiya is at the end of his rope. His mother is ill, and his job barely pays for her medication, much less food. With few options left, he considers the life-changing process of transfloration. Ready to give his body up for a payday, Kamiya is about to explore the limits of society's waning humanity.

Yasuda launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Big Comic Superior magazine in November 2020. Shogakukan released the manga's 13th compiled book volume on June 30, and will release the 14th on November 30.

The manga ranked #12 in the male reader list of the 2023 edition of Takarajimasha 's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! (This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook.

The television anime of the manga will premiere worldwide on Netflix on November 26. Atsuyuki Yukawa ( Suzume unit director) is directing the anime at Sunrise and SHAFT . Jin Tanaka ( Oshi no Ko ) is writing the script. Robert Satō is designing the characters. Tatsuya Katō ( Dr. Stone ) is composing the music.

title: Ingoku Danchi: Deviant's Apartment Complex Anime's English Dub Streams on November 11
content:
OceanVeil announced on Friday that it will begin streaming the English dub for Ingoku Danchi: Deviant's Apartment Complex , the short television anime of writer Sakusei Kenkyūjo and artist Yui Jōyama 's Ingoku Danchi (Indecent Apartment Complex) manga on November 11 at 11:00 p.m. EST.

The English dub cast inlcudes:

• Chloe Eves as Kiritani, Katagiri, Watanabe, Ichinose, Kanzaki, Sanamori

• Mana T. Johnson as Goda, Shikijo, Mizutani, Ikayama, Sakakura

• Shay-Ki Fullalove as Yoshida

• Christopher Escalante as Narrator

• Aria Pierce as Numajiri

• Jessica Warner as Shoda, Justice Man

• Abby Pasion as Hasegawa

• KyLeigh Zimmerer asTsujisaki

• Angela Tran as Shirakage

• Zoe Lee as Haibara

• Steve Warky Nunez as Yoshida's Dad

• Aife as Ando

• Khai Truong as Young Man

• Erin Tenelle as Boy, Housewife C

• Amanda Parker as Housewife A

• Rebecca Trepanier as Housewife B, NTR Wife

• Savy Des-Etages as Housewife D

• Jesse Inocalla as Mizutani's Husband, NTR Husband

• Christiaan Connors as Male Resident, Old Man, Man A

• Meredith Nudo as Horny Houswife

• Zack Maher as Horny Househusband

• KyLeigh Zimmerer, Erin Tenelle, Nina Nikolic, Zoe Lee, Rebecca Trepanier, Savy Des-Etages, Roo Ryder as Housewives

• Dré Ayala, Jesse Inocalla, Khai Truong, Steve Warky Nunez as Househusbands

OceanVeil describes the anime:

"Protect the peace of the complex from the threat of deviant housewives, Rookie Manager Yoshida!"

When Yoshida stepped in as his father's substitute manager for the apartment complex, he expected leaky faucets and noisy neighbors. Instead, he found a living nightmare of high-rise proportions!

The local housewives have traded their aprons for the "Libido Cloth"—lewd, madness-inducing garments that have turned the hallways into a frenzy of forbidden desires. From the chaotic rampages of residents like Watanabe and Ichinose to the looming, high-class threat of the "Class-A Housewife" Kanzaki, the darkness in the complex is deepening—and even the police shadows seem to be hiding something sinister.

Armed with his only counter-measure, the "Voltac Claw," Yoshida is the last line of defense. Can one rookie manager survive the onslaught, or will he be swallowed whole by the apartment's deepest secrets?

Toshikatsu Tokoro ( The Highschool Life of a Fudanshi , Plus-Sized Elf , Why the Hell are You Here, Teacher!? ) directed the anime at Elias . Eeyo Kurosaki ( Ichigo Aika: Strawberry Elegy , The Titan's Bride , Unexpectedly Naughty Fukami ) was in charge of series scripts, Shingo Nishimoto ( Plus-Sized Elf , The Fruit of Evolution 2: Before I Knew It, My Life Had It Made , chief animation director) designed the characters, and Ruzarin Kashiwagi composed the music.

Additional staff members include:

• Color Key Artist: Shūichi Satō

• Art Director: Shinobu Takahashi

• Compositing Director of Photography: Yoshikazu Miyagawa

• Sound Director: Akinori Shiba

The anime premiered in Japan on April 5 on BS11 at 25:10 JST (effectively April 6 at 1:10 a.m.), then on April 7 on Tokyo MX . AnimeFesta exclusively streams the anime's completely uncensored version in Japan, and also streams the on-air version with DMM TV . The anime's standard broadcast version and fully uncensored version debuted on WWWave Corporation 's new anime streaming platform OceanVeil on April 5.

The manga launched on Kadokawa 's Dra Dra Sharp# online manga magazine on the Nico Nico Seiga service in 2021. Kadokawa published the manga's ninth compiled book volume on February 9.

title: 10 Best Anime to Binge on Crunchyroll in November 2026
content:
The final quarter of the year has already begun, and there’s no surprise that Crunchyroll is bringing all the major series to its library. As the largest streaming platform for anime fans across the world, Crunchyroll offers an exciting range of series across all genres. The Fall 2026 anime season brings a new lineup of exciting shows on the platform. There’s no denying that the sequel seasons of The Apothecary Diaries and Black Clover grabbed all the spotlight this quarter. However, since this season’s anime were released only this month, there aren’t enough episodes for fans to binge.

New series within the seasonal lineup broadcast weekly episodes in Japan, after which Crunchyroll adds them to its library for fans across the globe. Not to mention that keeping up with weekly episodes isn’t ideal for those who prefer binge-watching, especially during the weekends when someone just needs a break after a long week. It’s also overwhelming to keep up with the updates since most episodes tend to end on a cliffhanger and make fans wait for several days before revealing what happens next. If you’re looking to watch new anime shows this month that have already released full seasons, then this list is perfect for you.

10) Release that Witch

Release that Witch is technically a donghua, a term used to describe Chinese animation series. The Chinese animation industry has been on the rise for the past few years, and a lot of the notable series end up on Crunchyroll. Among the donghua on the platform, Release that Witch is one of the most underrated ones, but it’s worth a watch for every adventure fantasy fan. One of the reasons why the series stands out is that it maintains a serious, grounded tone and skips out on cheap gags or exaggerated anime reactions. The story follows a modern engineer who transmigrates into a prince named Ronald Wimbledon and relies on logic and science instead of possessing some overpowered ability. Additionally, the story also steers away from the stereotypical portrayal of witches in fiction as women ostracized from everyone else. Instead, this series features how they are integrated into society as they use their powers for construction and engineering.

9) Yuri!!! on Ice

Despite the prequel film’s cancellation in April 2024, MAPPA’s original anime Yuri!!! on Ice still has a wide global fan base. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the anime, and while MAPPA had several surprises planned for fans, especially in Japan, nothing was related to the anime’s continuation. Regardless of the cancellation, the story ends on a rather impressive note, and it could be considered a fairly satisfying conclusion. Even if you’re not a beginner, it’s a perfect time to jog your memory as you rewatch this all-time classic. The story centers around Yuri Katsuki, a figure skater who returns to Japan after a crushing defeat at the Grand Prix Finale. Just when he’s decided to give up on his career as a figure skater, Victor Nikiforov, a five-time world champion, offers to become his coach after watching Yuri’s viral video. Eagerly accepting the offer from his idol, Yuri prepares himself for the fierce competition so he can take the gold medal home.

8) Mob Psycho 100

Mob Psycho 100 is often considered among the best Shonen series of all time, thanks to the exceptional story, stunning animation, fight choreography, and a satisfying ending. The anime wraps up the captivating story within three seasons, giving viewers everything they could ask for in a Shonen anime. Based on ONE’s award-winning manga, the same author as One-Punch Man , the story centers around Shigeo Kageyama, also known as Mob, an eighth-grade student with destructive psychic abilities who decides to keep his powers hidden from the world. In order to keep his powers honed, he works under Arataka Reigen, a scam artist who wants to make use of Mob’s terrifying abilities. Just as Arataka wanted, Mob fights evil spirits for him while using his powers under the guise of training. However, the troubles surrounding him never cease to exist. The anime is commemorating its 10th anniversary this year, making it the perfect time to watch this beloved show.

7) Black Clover

After making fans wait for five years, Black Clover is all set to return with a second season in a few days. While the manga has already reached its conclusion this year, the anime will continue the beloved Spade Kingdom Arc. When it comes to the main themes of the story, there are more differences than similarities, but Black Clover also follows an underdog protagonist who happens to be the only one in the world unable to use magic. In a world where magic is everything, Asta grew up in an orphanage in a small village. He spent his childhood dreaming of becoming the Wizard King, a title granted only to the most powerful mage in the kingdom. Unlike him, another boy from the same orphanage, Yuno, is considered a rare prodigy even among the high-ranking nobles. Despite the difference in their abilities, the boys set their sights on becoming the Wizard King, a title granted to the strongest Magic Knight in the Clover Kingdom.

6) Samurai Champloo

Directed by the legendary Shinichirō Watanabe, this 2004 classic is still ahead of its time, whether it’s the animation style or the hip-hop soundtrack in the Edo-themed story. Even more than two decades later, this beloved anime is still considered one of the greatest historical action series of all time . However, the anime wasn’t an overnight mainstream juggernaut upon its release, but instead gained fame over the years, and it’s something everyone should watch regardless of whether they’re an anime fan or not. The anime is largely episodic in nature, where each episode feels like a self-contained adventure as they build character depth and continue the central quest to find the mysterious samurai who smells like flowers. This incredible story is based on a short manga series written and illustrated by Masaru Gotsubo. Even though some of the anime episodes are fillers, these original scenes only add more depth to the main trio, Mugen, Jin, and Fuu, as they embark on a journey to find a Samurai who smells of sunflowers.

5) Dr. Stone

2026 was a bittersweet year for Dr. Stone fans as the anime finally reached its conclusion several years after its debut. Even among post-apocalyptic series, Dr. Stone stands out for having a unique setting and premise of the story. The anime is based on the award-winning Shonen Jump manga written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi. It’s one of those series that you just can’t find a replacement for thanks to its exceptional story. The story takes place 3700 years after a bizarre event that petrified all of humanity. Long after everything humanity built over time had vanished, Senku Ishigami wakes up from his slumber and embarks on a mission to rebuild civilization. The anime blends real-life scientific intrigue into the plot and weaves together a series of exciting events that help the characters revive humanity in the stone world.

4) Natsume’s Book of Friends

With the Fall season approaching us, it’s the perfect time of the year to watch this masterpiece. The story is set in a countryside filled with lush forests, old shrines, dusty roads at sunset, and it’s not just soothing to the eyes, but also to your soul. This bittersweet anime explores themes of making peace with your past and forming new bonds while also focusing on trauma, loneliness, and grief. As a supernatural fantasy centring on Yokai, the story doesn’t focus on horror but offers bittersweet encounters with these yokai and their stories. The series is episodic in nature as it centers around Tatsuki Natsume and his Yokai companion who encounter new allies and enemies along the way. The anime is based on an ongoing manga by Yuki Midorikawa, and it has released seven seasons already. While there have been no updates on Season 8 so far, all the available seasons are enough to keep you busy for a few days.

3) Witch Hat Atelier

This beloved fantasy anime has only aired its first season, and it’s already considered one of the biggest hits in recent years. Thanks to the striking visuals and the unique fantasy setting, the anime will draw you in right away. The anime is based on an award-winning manga written and illustrated by Kamone Shirahama, which has been serialized in Kodansha’s seinen magazine Morning Two since 2016. The stellar visuals do justice to the manga’s intricate art style, even though adapting a series with such a unique style into another medium is always more complicated. Since the manga is long and more detailed, the anime had to make a few changes, including removing certain scenes to fit into the episodes. Even so, the adaptation has been nothing short of extraordinary. However, it’s not just the animation and art style, but the story itself is intriguing enough to keep fans immersed in Coco’s journey as she uncovers the truth about the world of magic.

2) Journal the Witch

Unlike what the title suggests, Journal the Witch is not a supernatural fantasy. In fact, the witch in the title is a metaphor for the main characters’ perceived differences from social norms, instead of an actual magical power. Although the anime is critically acclaimed, it remains one of the most underrated series of the year. This must be why the anime hasn’t been renewed for a second season yet, even though the manga has more than enough material to begin production. The story centers around a 35-year-old novelist, Makio Kodai, who takes in her 15-year-old niece after the girl’s parents died in an accident. The anime follows their journey as they learn to live with each other while figuring out what they must do in their lives. The story portrays real-life struggles through the characters, making it all the more relatable as the main characters form an unbreakable bond.

1) Spy x Family

Based on Tatsuya Endo’s beloved Shonen Jump+ manga, Spy x Family returned with its Season 3 last year, which you can catch up on the series while awaiting updates on Season 4. Although the anime hasn’t officially announced a fourth season yet, considering its popularity, it’s more or less guaranteed the studio will release it eventually. The third season brings Loid one step closer to completing Operation Strix, but the mission is turning out to be more difficult than even he can handle. This beloved anime blends spy action and the found family tropes into an epic journey of the unique Forger family. The series is episodic in nature as the story keeps progressing slowly towards the end goal. Not only that, but despite having a comedic appeal, the series has deep and complex undertones focusing on war, grief, human experimentation, among many other dark themes.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

contentBlocks.text: The final quarter of the year has already begun, and there’s no surprise that Crunchyroll is bringing all the major series to its library. As the largest streaming platform for anime fans across the world, Crunchyroll offers an exciting range of series across all genres. The Fall 2026 anime season brings a new lineup of exciting shows on the platform. There’s no denying that the sequel seasons of The Apothecary Diaries and Black Clover grabbed all the spotlight this quarter. However, since this season’s anime were released only this month, there aren’t enough episodes for fans to binge.

New series within the seasonal lineup broadcast weekly episodes in Japan, after which Crunchyroll adds them to its library for fans across the globe. Not to mention that keeping up with weekly episodes isn’t ideal for those who prefer binge-watching, especially during the weekends when someone just needs a break after a long week. It’s also overwhelming to keep up with the updates since most episodes tend to end on a cliffhanger and make fans wait for several days before revealing what happens next. If you’re looking to watch new anime shows this month that have already released full seasons, then this list is perfect for you.
10) Release that Witch

Release that Witch is technically a donghua, a term used to describe Chinese animation series. The Chinese animation industry has been on the rise for the past few years, and a lot of the notable series end up on Crunchyroll. Among the donghua on the platform, Release that Witch is one of the most underrated ones, but it’s worth a watch for every adventure fantasy fan. One of the reasons why the series stands out is that it maintains a serious, grounded tone and skips out on cheap gags or exaggerated anime reactions. The story follows a modern engineer who transmigrates into a prince named Ronald Wimbledon and relies on logic and science instead of possessing some overpowered ability. Additionally, the story also steers away from the stereotypical portrayal of witches in fiction as women ostracized from everyone else. Instead, this series features how they are integrated into society as they use their powers for construction and engineering.
9) Yuri!!! on Ice

Despite the prequel film’s cancellation in April 2024, MAPPA’s original anime Yuri!!! on Ice still has a wide global fan base. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the anime, and while MAPPA had several surprises planned for fans, especially in Japan, nothing was related to the anime’s continuation. Regardless of the cancellation, the story ends on a rather impressive note, and it could be considered a fairly satisfying conclusion. Even if you’re not a beginner, it’s a perfect time to jog your memory as you rewatch this all-time classic. The story centers around Yuri Katsuki, a figure skater who returns to Japan after a crushing defeat at the Grand Prix Finale. Just when he’s decided to give up on his career as a figure skater, Victor Nikiforov, a five-time world champion, offers to become his coach after watching Yuri’s viral video. Eagerly accepting the offer from his idol, Yuri prepares himself for the fierce competition so he can take the gold medal home.
8) Mob Psycho 100

Mob Psycho 100 is often considered among the best Shonen series of all time, thanks to the exceptional story, stunning animation, fight choreography, and a satisfying ending. The anime wraps up the captivating story within three seasons, giving viewers everything they could ask for in a Shonen anime. Based on ONE’s award-winning manga, the same author as One-Punch Man , the story centers around Shigeo Kageyama, also known as Mob, an eighth-grade student with destructive psychic abilities who decides to keep his powers hidden from the world. In order to keep his powers honed, he works under Arataka Reigen, a scam artist who wants to make use of Mob’s terrifying abilities. Just as Arataka wanted, Mob fights evil spirits for him while using his powers under the guise of training. However, the troubles surrounding him never cease to exist. The anime is commemorating its 10th anniversary this year, making it the perfect time to watch this beloved show.
7) Black Clover

After making fans wait for five years, Black Clover is all set to return with a second season in a few days. While the manga has already reached its conclusion this year, the anime will continue the beloved Spade Kingdom Arc. When it comes to the main themes of the story, there are more differences than similarities, but Black Clover also follows an underdog protagonist who happens to be the only one in the world unable to use magic. In a world where magic is everything, Asta grew up in an orphanage in a small village. He spent his childhood dreaming of becoming the Wizard King, a title granted only to the most powerful mage in the kingdom. Unlike him, another boy from the same orphanage, Yuno, is considered a rare prodigy even among the high-ranking nobles. Despite the difference in their abilities, the boys set their sights on becoming the Wizard King, a title granted to the strongest Magic Knight in the Clover Kingdom.
6) Samurai Champloo

Directed by the legendary Shinichirō Watanabe, this 2004 classic is still ahead of its time, whether it’s the animation style or the hip-hop soundtrack in the Edo-themed story. Even more than two decades later, this beloved anime is still considered one of the greatest historical action series of all time . However, the anime wasn’t an overnight mainstream juggernaut upon its release, but instead gained fame over the years, and it’s something everyone should watch regardless of whether they’re an anime fan or not. The anime is largely episodic in nature, where each episode feels like a self-contained adventure as they build character depth and continue the central quest to find the mysterious samurai who smells like flowers. This incredible story is based on a short manga series written and illustrated by Masaru Gotsubo. Even though some of the anime episodes are fillers, these original scenes only add more depth to the main trio, Mugen, Jin, and Fuu, as they embark on a journey to find a Samurai who smells of sunflowers.
5) Dr. Stone

2026 was a bittersweet year for Dr. Stone fans as the anime finally reached its conclusion several years after its debut. Even among post-apocalyptic series, Dr. Stone stands out for having a unique setting and premise of the story. The anime is based on the award-winning Shonen Jump manga written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi. It’s one of those series that you just can’t find a replacement for thanks to its exceptional story. The story takes place 3700 years after a bizarre event that petrified all of humanity. Long after everything humanity built over time had vanished, Senku Ishigami wakes up from his slumber and embarks on a mission to rebuild civilization. The anime blends real-life scientific intrigue into the plot and weaves together a series of exciting events that help the characters revive humanity in the stone world.
4) Natsume’s Book of Friends

With the Fall season approaching us, it’s the perfect time of the year to watch this masterpiece. The story is set in a countryside filled with lush forests, old shrines, dusty roads at sunset, and it’s not just soothing to the eyes, but also to your soul. This bittersweet anime explores themes of making peace with your past and forming new bonds while also focusing on trauma, loneliness, and grief. As a supernatural fantasy centring on Yokai, the story doesn’t focus on horror but offers bittersweet encounters with these yokai and their stories. The series is episodic in nature as it centers around Tatsuki Natsume and his Yokai companion who encounter new allies and enemies along the way. The anime is based on an ongoing manga by Yuki Midorikawa, and it has released seven seasons already. While there have been no updates on Season 8 so far, all the available seasons are enough to keep you busy for a few days.
3) Witch Hat Atelier

This beloved fantasy anime has only aired its first season, and it’s already considered one of the biggest hits in recent years. Thanks to the striking visuals and the unique fantasy setting, the anime will draw you in right away. The anime is based on an award-winning manga written and illustrated by Kamone Shirahama, which has been serialized in Kodansha’s seinen magazine Morning Two since 2016. The stellar visuals do justice to the manga’s intricate art style, even though adapting a series with such a unique style into another medium is always more complicated. Since the manga is long and more detailed, the anime had to make a few changes, including removing certain scenes to fit into the episodes. Even so, the adaptation has been nothing short of extraordinary. However, it’s not just the animation and art style, but the story itself is intriguing enough to keep fans immersed in Coco’s journey as she uncovers the truth about the world of magic.
2) Journal the Witch

Unlike what the title suggests, Journal the Witch is not a supernatural fantasy. In fact, the witch in the title is a metaphor for the main characters’ perceived differences from social norms, instead of an actual magical power. Although the anime is critically acclaimed, it remains one of the most underrated series of the year. This must be why the anime hasn’t been renewed for a second season yet, even though the manga has more than enough material to begin production. The story centers around a 35-year-old novelist, Makio Kodai, who takes in her 15-year-old niece after the girl’s parents died in an accident. The anime follows their journey as they learn to live with each other while figuring out what they must do in their lives. The story portrays real-life struggles through the characters, making it all the more relatable as the main characters form an unbreakable bond.
1) Spy x Family

Based on Tatsuya Endo’s beloved Shonen Jump+ manga, Spy x Family returned with its Season 3 last year, which you can catch up on the series while awaiting updates on Season 4. Although the anime hasn’t officially announced a fourth season yet, considering its popularity, it’s more or less guaranteed the studio will release it eventually. The third season brings Loid one step closer to completing Operation Strix, but the mission is turning out to be more difficult than even he can handle. This beloved anime blends spy action and the found family tropes into an epic journey of the unique Forger family. The series is episodic in nature as the story keeps progressing slowly towards the end goal. Not only that, but despite having a comedic appeal, the series has deep and complex undertones focusing on war, grief, human experimentation, among many other dark themes.

title: Live-Action My Sister's Boyfriend Film's Clip Shows Sui, Midori Rescuing Dog
content:
The official website for My Sister's Boyfriend , the live-action film of Amu Meguro 's Midori Loves My Sister ( Onē-chan no Midori-kun or literally My sister's Midori-kun ) manga, presented a new clip from the film on Monday. The clip shows Sui and Midori rescuing an abandoned dog that Sui discovers on the way home from school.

The original manga centers on Sui, a girl in her third year of junior high. She doesn't really get along with her older sister's boyfriend, Midori-kun, since he always treats her like a kid and makes fun of her. But Midori-kun is suddenly asked to be Sui's home tutor, and she suddenly sees an unexpected side of him.

The film has the English title My Sister's Boyfriend , and stars timelesz idol group member Masaki Hashimoto (live-action Summer Complicity ) as Midori Yukishiro, and actress Runa Nakajima (live-action Uchi no Otōto-domo ga Sumimasen ) as Sui Sanae. Rinka Kumada (live-action Otonanajimi , Kimi ni Todoke , It Takes More than a Pretty Face to Fall in Love ) plays Sui's older sister and Midori's girlfriend Momo Sanae, and Reo Matsumoto (live-action I Cannot Reach You , Propaganda Game ) plays Sui's childhood friend Ayame Mizukawa. Taisuke Niihara (live-action At 25:00 in Akasaka , Young & Fine ) plays Amamiya, a new assistant producer at the same TV station where Sui's older sister Momo works.

Mahito Kimura (live-action Strobe Edge , Blue Spring Ride series) is directing the film, and Nami Kikkawa (live-action Honey Lemon Soda film) wrote the script. Shochiku is credited for planning and overseeing the production, and is also distributing the film. timelesz performs the film's theme song "Hontō no Koto o Iu to" (If I Tell the Truth).

The film will open in Japan on December 4.

Meguro launched the manga in Shueisha 's Bessatsu Margaret magazine in 2022. Shueisha published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on April 23.

Meguro ended the Hinata no Blue manga in July 2021. Meguro launched the manga in Bessatsu Margaret in April 2019.

Meguro's Honey So Sweet manga ran in Bessatsu Margaret from August 2012 to November 2015. Viz Media 's Shojo Beat imprint has released the eight-volume manga in English. The series was ranked as one of Japanese Bookstore Employees' top recommended comics for 2014. The manga inspired a live-action film adaptation that opened in Japan in March 2018.

title: Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Just Made the Original Ending Tragic & Fans May Have Missed It
content:
Several years after the original story’s ending, Solo Leveling: Ragnarok decides to make it more tragic than ever. The webtoon returned this month with Season 3 after more than ten months of hiatus following the lead artist JIN’s enlistment in the mandatatory military service. The series returns with a new artist and more exciting plot twists and Suho’s journey continues. However, the series also focuses on original characters from the main story written by Chugong. Solo Leveling: Ragnarok serves as a spin-off or a parallel-universe story rather than a continuation of the main story, which is why the novel’s author Daul took liberties into changing many things about the series.

While the webtoon is not even halfway over, the novel has long since concluded. The series continues to get even more intense in the latest season , especially since fans waited several months to see the story answer major questions about the world. Three chapters were released at once during the third season’s launch, which brought back Cha Haein, one of th most beloved characters from the original. She was introduced in the main story as an S-Rank Hunter and later married Jinwoo and gave birth to Suho. The series reveals its own version of the original ending that made the series more tragic than ever.

Solo Leveling: Ragnarok Confirms a Tragic Ending for Jinwoo and Haein

The original series ended on a bittersweet note after the time reset when Jinwoo and Haein celebrated their 16th anniversary. While Haein naturally grew old as time passed, Jinwoo kept changing his appearance since he was practically immortal after inheriting the full powers of Ashborn. Even so, he made it look like the two of them grew old together. The couple also shared a romantic ride together on Kaisel’s back just as they did during their first date. The story ends as they share an embrace before Jinwoo could fight new enemies threatening his world. However, Ragnarok confirms that the joyful ride was only the beginning of the tragedy because left her behind and never returned.

They made a promise to see each other again and Haein keeps waiting for him to this day. The embrace they shared on the original ending was actually the last one before they were separated forever. While Jinwoo went off to fight the Apostles of Itarim after separating from his wife, Haein got swallowed up by an S-Rank Gate and remained trapped in the Land of the Snowfolk ever since. Both of them were never able to make it home to see their son ever again. While the original ending tells the story from Jinwoo’s perspective, Ragnarok focuses on Haein, which is all the more reason why the story became even more tragic now. She reawakened her powers as an S-Rank Hunter again and is now stronger than ever. Haein was reunited with her fellow S-Rank Hunters in Ragnarok as the mother and son’s seems inevitable at this point.

Do you think Solo Leveling ’s original ending hits differently after the latest chapters in Ragnarok, and what did you make of this unexpected plot twist? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

title: Gen Hoshino Performs Hirayasumi TV Anime's Opening Song
content:
The website for the television anime of Keigo Shinzō 's Hirayasumi manga (a co-production with Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions Co., Ltd and Production +h. ) announced on Monday that Gen Hoshino is performing the anime's opening theme song. The announcement did not reveal the song's title.

Viz Media describes the human drama story:

With a carefree outlook on life, Hiroto knows better than anyone that slowing down is sometimes the best way to move forward. At 29 years old, carefree Hiroto Ikuta doesn't have a girlfriend, a full-time job, or a plan for the future—and he couldn't be happier. Hiroto's breezy attitude isn't easy for everyone to understand, though. In a world filled with anxiety, confusion, and grief, Hiroto and the people who surround him are all just doing their best to figure out this thing called life. After developing an unlikely friendship with the grouchy old woman who lives in his neighborhood, Hiroto suddenly finds himself inheriting not just her house but some rather difficult emotions as well. His 18-year-old cousin, Natsumi, moves in with him, but as a struggling art student, she has her own troubles to deal with and may just put Hiroto's easygoing lifestyle to the test.

The anime stars :

• Yūma Uchida as Hiroto Ikuta

• Mayu Takahashi as Natsumi Kobayashi

• Rikako Aikawa as Hanae Wada

• Daisuke Namikawa as Hideki Noguchi

• Yōko Hikasa as Yomogi Tachibana

• Yume Miyamoto as Akari Yokoyama

• Yūichirō Umehara as Ryō Ishikawa

• Japanese television announcer Yūko Naitō as Narrator

Kei Suezawa ( Fate/Grand Order The Movie Divine Realm of the Round Table: Camelot - Wandering: Agateram , FLCL Progressive ) is directing the anime at Production +h. Naoyuki Asano (2022 Urusei Yatsura , Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! , Mr. Osomatsu ) is designing the characters. Mika Nishimura ( Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction , Typhoon Noruda ) is the art director. Kaori Sawada ( What Did You Eat Yesterday? , When Spring Comes ) is composing the music. TOMOO will perform the anime's ending theme song "Fūmizekka" (Delicious Flavor).

The anime will premiere in January 2027 in Japan on the NHK General channel. Viz Media also announced an English release in 2027.

Viz Media and Japan Society hosted the world premiere screening of the first episode at Japan Society's location in New York City on October 7.

Shinzō launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Weekly Big Comic Spirits magazine in April 2021. Shogakukan published the manga's 10th compiled book volume on April 30, and the series has over 1.1 million copies in circulation worldwide. The manga will end on November 16.

The manga was nominated for the 15th Manga Taisho awards in January 2022, ranked #18 in the 2023 edition of Takarajimasha 's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! (This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook in December 2022, was nominated for the 27th Annual Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize in February 2023, and was nominated for Best Continuing Manga Series in the 2nd American Manga Awards.

The manga also inspired a live-action series , which premiered on NHK in November 2025.

Denpa has licensed Shinzō's Holiday Junction collection of short manga. The book contains seven one-shot manga. Shogakukan shipped the book in Japan in July 2016.

title: My Crush’s Crush Anime Reveals Teaser Visual, Trailer, Staff, Cast, April 2027 Premiere
content:
The previously announced My Crush’s Crush anime revealed a teaser visual and a trailer on Monday. The main staff and cast and an April 2027 premiere date, have also been announced. Studio project No.9 is in charge of the animation.

Kazuomi Koga is directing the anime with Yoriko Tomita handling the series scripts. Takayuki Noguchi is designing the characters, and Rina Tayama is composing the music. The main cast includes:

• Gakuto Kajiwara as Sora Akizuki

• Haruna Mikawa as Asahi Suzukaze

• Nene Hieda as Miya Fuwa

The anime is based on a manga written by Sekina Aoi and illustrated by Ryo Tsuzura. It is currently serialized in Hakusensha’s Young Animal ZERO . Yen Press is licensing the title in English, describing it as follows: When Sora Akizuki confesses his feelings to Miya Fuwa, he gets rejected outright. As it turns out, she likes Asahi Suzukaze, the president of the mysterious “Clinical Trials Club.” When he joins the club to learn more about Asahi, he discovers that she also has a crush on someone else! Could this chain of crushes get any more complicated…? Source: My Crush’s Crush anime Official website , X (formerly Twitter) © Sekina Aoi, Tsuzura Ryo/Hakusensha/”The Person I Like” Production Committee

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Earns Record $32 Million in N. American Opening Weekend
content:
Godzilla Minus Zero , the new Godzilla sequel film from Godzilla Minus One 's Takashi Yamazaki , earned an estimated US$31.61 million at the North American box office in its opening weekend. A record 74% of that total came from premium large format screenings, with 40% or US$12 million from IMAX screenings. (It is the first Japanese film to meet the standard to advertise itself as "filmed for IMAX.")

This is the highest ever U.S. opening weekend for a GKIDS release (higher than The Boy and the Heron 's US$13 million in 2023 ), as well as the highest one ever for a live-action foreign film. (The highest one for a foreign film is still the first Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle anime film with US$70.6 million, unadjusted for inflation, in September 2025. The English dub of Pokémon: The First Movie opened with US$50.8 million in its first five days in July 1998.)

Godzilla Minus Zero 's global revenue stands at US$63 million after its opening weekend. Deadline reports it was the highest-grossing film in the world this past weekend.

The film earned 590,000 tickets for 910 million yen (about US$5.75 million) in Japan in its opening day alone, setting a new record for the highest opening day earnings for a live-action film (among both foreign and domestic live-action films) in Japan. The film had 201% higher opening day earnings than its predecessor Godzilla Minus One in Japan.

The film opened in Japan on Tuesday, November 3, which is "Godzilla Day" in Japan, celebrating the anniversary of the first Godzilla film's November 3, 1954 release. Godzilla Minus One similarly opened in Japan on November 3, 2023. (Godzilla Day fell on a Tuesday this year, but it is also the Japanese holiday known as Culture Day.)

The sequel is set in 1949, two years after the Godzilla Minus One film's story.

Min Tanaka ( 47 Ronin , live-action Rurouni Kenshin films) plays biologist Kanji Murakami. He joined returning cast members Ryūnosuke Kamiki (Koichi Shikishima), Minami Hamabe (Noriko Ōishi), and Hidetaka Yoshioka (Noda) from Godzilla Minus One . Also returning in the cast are Yūki Yamada (Shiro Mizushima), Kuranosuke Sasaki (Seiji Akitsu), Sakura Andō (Sumiko Ota), and Miō Tanaka (Tatsuo Ho tta).

Yamazaki returned as director, screenwriter, and VFX supervisor. Naoki Satō also returned to compose the music. Shirogumi Inc. handled the film's visual effects.

GKIDS and TOHO released the film in North America on Friday, November 6. This is the first time a Japan-produced Godzilla film opened in Japan and in North America in the same week.

In addition to opening in Japan and North America, it opened in the same week in Latin America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Australia, and New Zealand. The companies stated they would announce additional international release dates at a later time. TOHO acquired GKIDS in October 2024.

Godzilla Minus One has earned more than US$116 million worldwide. According to Box Office Mojo, the film has earned an estimated US$57,144,669 in the United States. The film was the third highest-grossing foreign-language film in the United States as of 2024.

Netflix is streaming the film and Godzilla Minus One /Minus Color , the black-and-white version of the film, worldwide on Netflix . In North America, Godzilla Minus One and Godzilla Minus One /Minus Color are additionally available for digital rental and digital purchase on Amazon, Apple iTunes , Google Play , Microsoft , FandangoNOW/ VUDU , inDemand, XBOX, and Vubiquity. In Japan, the film is streaming exclusively (in color and monochrome) on Amazon Prime Video .

Godzilla Minus One won the Best Visual Effects award in the 96th Academy Awards in March 2024. The film is the first Japanese film to win in this category, and the first Godzilla film to be nominated for an Oscar.

Yamazaki's first English-language film Grandgear was originally slated to open on February 18, 2028, but Sony Pictures recently moved up its release date to January 14, 2028.
